summary.text: The accepted statement is merely the proposition \(\mathrm{True}\), so the proof is the immediate tautological observation that \(\mathrm{True}\) holds; it contains no number-theoretic argument.

full_proof.text:
The proposition to be proved is \(\mathrm{True}\).

By definition, \(\mathrm{True}\) is the proposition that holds unconditionally: it has a canonical proof requiring no hypotheses, witnesses, constructions, reductions, or case distinctions. Taking that canonical proof establishes \(\mathrm{True}\), and hence proves the stated theorem.
